# CMS content governance checklist

## Purpose

Use this checklist to keep website content accurate, accessible, owned, and maintainable. Adapt it to the organization, CMS, publishing risk, and legal requirements.

## Ownership and inventory

- [ ] Identify the site's audiences, important content, languages, and content owner.
- [ ] Keep a useful inventory of important published and draft content.
- [ ] Give important content an owner and review date.
- [ ] Find duplicate, expired, inaccurate, test, unused, and ownerless content.
- [ ] Decide whether outdated content should be updated, combined, redirected, archived, or deleted.

## Roles and publishing

- [ ] Define who can write, review, approve, publish, translate, and administer content.
- [ ] Give each person the lowest CMS permissions they need.
- [ ] Remove stale accounts and avoid shared publishing accounts.
- [ ] Define a publishing workflow that fits the risk of the content.
- [ ] Require extra review for legal, financial, safety, policy, or crisis content.
- [ ] Document how urgent corrections and emergency publishing work.

## Content structure and quality

- [ ] Define useful content types, fields, taxonomies, relationships, and URL rules.
- [ ] Make CMS field labels, instructions, previews, and errors understandable to editors.
- [ ] Explain how shared, reused, translated, personalized, and external content is updated.
- [ ] Write simple standards for headings, links, calls to action, dates, media, downloads, and voice.
- [ ] Confirm templates support accessible headings, links, images, tables, captions, and documents.
- [ ] Review content on the actual page, not only in the CMS editor.
- [ ] Check accuracy, spelling, links, metadata, permissions, and accessibility before publishing.

## Maintenance and recovery

- [ ] Review time-sensitive and high-value content on a schedule or after important events.
- [ ] Preserve useful URLs and redirect moved content to the closest replacement.
- [ ] Define retention, archival, deletion, and legal-hold rules where required.
- [ ] Test drafting, previewing, approval, publishing, scheduling, correction, and unpublishing.
- [ ] Back up the content, media, redirects, approvals, and configuration needed for recovery.
- [ ] Prevent environment synchronization from overwriting newer production content.
- [ ] Assign owners for editor training, documentation, access reviews, and content audits.

## References
